title: Why You Keep Forgetting to Cancel Free Trials (On Purpose)
alts: The Real Reason 'Free Trials' Need Your Credit Card
You Forgot to Cancel Your Free Trial. That Was the Plan.
line1: Why do free trials always need your credit card? Dave signed up for a 'free' week and got charged $14.99 a month for 5 months.
summary: Dave signs up for a 'free' 7-day trial, forgets about it, and gets charged $14.99 a month for five months before he notices. We break down why 'free' always needs a card number, the economics of 'breakage' revenue and forgotten app subscriptions, why auto-renew defaults to ON (the behavioral 'default effect'), why the intro price is never the real price, dark-pattern cancel mazes (including the NY AG's case against SiriusXM), the FTC's Click-to-Cancel rule and its 2025 court vacatur, state auto-renewal laws like California's, and the $2.5 billion Amazon Prime 'Iliad Flow' settlement. Then: how to trial anything with a virtual card, a calendar reminder, and an immediate cancel, without losing a single day of access.
